                    ### Question
                    35-year-old woman on hormonal treatment for infertility. He went to the emergency department due to constitutional syndrome and paresthesias in the left side of the body. In blood tests, Hb 7.5 g / dL, reticulocytes 10% (0.52%), platelets 5,000 / uL, normal leukocytes, LDH 1,200 IU / L, direct negative Coombs test, undetectable haptoglobin are detected. Morphology of peripheral blood with abundant schistocytes. Normal coagulation tests. What is the diagnostic suspicion and the most appropriate treatment?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Autoimmune hemolytic anemia. Start steroids.
opb. Von Willebrand disease. Administration of desmopressin.
opc. Thrombocytopenic purpura. Start steroids and platelet transfusion.
opd. Evans syndrome. Start steroids.
ope. Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura. Treatment with plasmapheresis.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's presentation with schistocytes on peripheral blood smear, severe thrombocytopenia, and constitutional symptoms raises suspicion for thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP). Given the clinical findings and evidence paths linking schistocytes to TTP, the most appropriate treatment would be plasmapheresis for TTP.
